why: The reference output against which prompts 03-07 of the pre-Python-migration-fixes campaign, and every stage of the subsequent Python/SymPy port, are validated. Captured before any behavioural fix was applied.

git.commit_subject: Record commit SHA for prompt 01 in log and status board
git.note: This is the commit the *binary* was built from -- prompt 01's tip. The prompt-02 commit that adds this archive touches only validation/ and prompts/, no source, so it cannot change the emitted tree.

command.note: This is NOT the tool's default. --auto-symmetrize is the default and is ~26x slower for the same answer; see validation/README.md.

captured.run_label: run1 of the five-run non-determinism study (validation/NONDETERMINISM.md)
captured.wall_clock_note: Five sequential runs measured 50.94 / 62.39 / 51.31 / 71.22 / 47.28 s real and 45.31 / 46.86 / 45.26 / 47.79 / 44.63 s user on an otherwise loaded laptop; user CPU is the stable figure.

contents.autogenerated/: the full emitted tree from the run above
contents.run.log: the captured stdout+stderr of that run, verbatim (ANSI colour codes intact)
contents.warnings.txt: the warning set, ANSI codes and timestamps stripped
contents.counterterm-map.canonical.txt: the ** COUNTERTERM MAP section with each entry's print order canonicalised (validation/canonical_form.py --counterterm-map) -- the form that IS comparable between runs: one md5 across all five runs of the non-determinism study and the --auto-symmetrize run
contents.counterterm-map.sorted-lines.txt: the same section with the lines merely sorted -- kept for reference, NOT usable for comparison (four distinct md5s in five runs)
contents.signatures.json: the integrand signature multiset from validation/compare_autogenerated.py, with the RNG seed and points

dedup.note: issue I-05; diagnostic only, deliberately not acted on

signature_policy.source: validation/compare_autogenerated.py, the constants block at the top

derived_md5.note: counterterm_map_sorted_lines is NOT stable run to run -- four distinct values in five runs, because the variability is intra-line. counterterm_map_canonical IS stable: one value across five runs plus the --auto-symmetrize run. The two sorted value_/Wick_ md5s and compute_name_set are also stable. See validation/NONDETERMINISM.md.

auto_symmetrize_cross_check.signature_comparison_vs_canonical_run: 101 of 101 matched on the exact key; compute_* identical
auto_symmetrize_cross_check.text_difference_vs_canonical_run: 80 of 101 sorted `double value_` lines and 53 of 101 `double Wick_` lines differ textually; all 101 signatures nevertheless match. The symmetrizer builds differently-ordered but algebraically identical expression trees.
auto_symmetrize_cross_check.verdict: identical output for ~25x the cost; the study's claim is confirmed
